_readme: Audio credits manifest for A Tale of Yarn.
The game imports ZERO audio files. Every sound is synthesized at runtime by
src/game/audio/audio-engine.ts from the recipe table in sfx.ts, so 'credits'
is empty and is supposed to be empty.
This file exists as the GUARD for the first imported file somebody adds.
scripts/test-audio-credits.mts walks the shipped asset directories and fails
if it finds an audio file with no entry here, if an entry names a file that
does not exist, or if any licence is outside policy.allowed.
TO ADD AN IMPORTED SOUND you must do all three, or the test goes red:
1. add an entry to 'credits' below,
2. add the identical entry to AUDIO_CREDITS in src/game/audio/sfx.ts
(the in-bundle copy the credits panel renders from - the test asserts
the two are deep-equal, so they cannot drift),
3. make sure the licence is one of policy.allowed, verbatim.
Entry shape: { file, url, author, licence, note? }
file    - path from the repo root, forward slashes
url     - where it was obtained
author  - who made it
licence - verbatim from policy.allowed
note    - optional: edits made, required attribution string, etc.
'voiceModels' below is a SEPARATE list with its own policy. Those are the
neural TTS voices the villagers speak with. They are not imported audio
files - nothing under models/ is scanned by the walk - but they are
third-party trained weights that ship in the depot, so their provenance
belongs in the same manifest. They are kept out of 'credits' on purpose:
'credits' is deep-equality-checked against AUDIO_CREDITS in sfx.ts, which
is what the in-game credits panel renders, and a 63 MB ONNX file is not a
sound effect.

forbiddenPatterns.why: Commercial Steam release. NC forbids it outright.
Copyleft on a derivative in a closed-source build.
BBC Sound Effects are personal/educational/research use only.
Any pitch-shift, trim or mix is a derivative.

attribution.CC0-1.0: No attribution obligation. The entry is recorded anyway so provenance is auditable.
attribution.CC-BY-4.0: Attribution required. The manifest entry IS the attribution and the credits panel renders it.

scanNote: dist/ is not scanned: it is a build product of the directories above, and
scripts/ is not scanned because everything under it is generated test
fixture or audition evidence (piper_fixture, voice_fixture, whisper_fixture,
shots/audition) - all gitignored, none of it ships.

why: A Piper voice inherits the licence of the speech it was trained on, and
those licences vary wildly between voices in the same repository. The
bar here is the same one the SFX policy sets: commercially usable in a
paid Steam release, in the EU as well as the US, with no copyleft reach
into a closed-source build. Public-domain / CC0 training data clears it
outright. Anything needing a case-by-case reading does not.
The forbidden patterns in policy.forbiddenPatterns apply here too and
the guard checks them against these entries as well - NC in particular,
which is what disqualified the otherwise obvious female candidate.

voiceModels.role: male NPCs and the Evil King
voiceModels.author: rhasspy (Piper) — dataset: OHF-Voice/voice-datasets
voiceModels.note: MODEL_CARD states License: CC0. Dataset https://github.com/OHF-Voice/voice-datasets. Measured natural f0 99.6 Hz.

voiceModels.author: Piper voice by Bryce Beattie (https://brycebeattie.com/files/tts/) — dataset: LJ Speech, Linda Johnson via LibriVox
voiceModels.note: MODEL_CARD gives dataset https://keithito.com/LJ-Speech-Dataset/ with 'License: public domain'. The dataset page states verbatim: 'This dataset is in the public domain in the US (and most likely other countries as well). There are no restrictions on its use.' Source audio is LibriVox (public domain), text is Project Gutenberg. Measured natural f0 219.2 Hz, so it needs almost no resampling to sit in the female band.

voiceModelsRejected.why: NonCommercial AND ShareAlike. Two independent disqualifications for a paid, closed-source release. This is the voice most guides recommend for 'a female Piper voice' — recorded here so it does not get re-proposed.
The MODEL_CARD points at a bespoke challenge licence rather than naming terms. A licence that needs a lawyer to read is not 'unambiguously commercial-safe'.
The MODEL_CARD names no licence at all, only a repository to go and look in. Unresolved provenance fails the bar by definition.

Licence is CLEAN and this was the runner-up, not a rejection on legal grounds. Dropped on acoustics: measured natural f0 148 Hz, so reaching the female band needs a 1.11-1.59x resample — the same formant-dragging that made the single-model design sound like a sped-up man. ljspeech needs ~1.0x.
